sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:17

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:17:1
items.html:
The first light, which was at first below and rose upward, did not descend again: That is to say, it was explained above in the adjacent item that through the coupling of AB and SAG the bottom Hey descended from the place of the Tabur and descended to the Bina of Nekudim, which is the Peh of the general Rosh of YESHSUT and Nekudim, study it there. For then the GE that are in YESHSUT became, together with the AHP, which are the KHB of Nekudim, a single Rosh, and by this the Mochin of GAR [first three] were drawn to Nekudim. And the ARI informs us here that even so, the very lights of YESHSUT were not joined so as to be attached to their own AHP, which are the Nekudim. And this is what he says, that the first light that was there did not descend again, and remained there from the Tabur upward even after the second coupling. And this is for two reasons. The first is that then YESHSUT too joined once more with the Taamim [tastes] of SAG into a single degree; for the whole division of SAG into two halves — into the Taamim, which are reckoned as the AB of SAG and as the value of AVI, and into the Nekudot, which are the first light called YESHSUT that was below the Tabur, reckoned as the SAG of SAG, as above (page 397, the passage beginning “AVI”), study it there well — behold, this entire division was by reason of the association of YESHSUT with phase four, as was written there. And it turns out now, after phase four has descended again to her place, that there is no longer any difference between the Taamim and YESHSUT, and the two of them returned to a single degree as at first.
And the second reason is that the matter of the annulment of the boundary of the conclusion by the Parsa was only for the hour, and that is why it is called by the name of a breach. And after the lights descended below, it immediately closed again; and therefore YESHSUT cannot descend below the Parsa, even after the descent of the bottom Hey from there.
For she did not descend from there permanently. Therefore the Parsa remained in all its force, and YESHSUT remained permanently above the Tabur, and only its illumination reaches downward, to complete the GAR of Nekudim.
